title: Change in Quantity to 10: 1 or 2 More and Less
seo_title: Kindergarten Change in quantity to 10 Worksheets: Free Math with Pictures and Answers (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: Change in quantity to 10, using concrete materials: generalizing change by adding 1 or 2; modeling and describing number relationships through change
meta_desc: Free Kindergarten math worksheets on change in quantity to 10 for the BC curriculum: 1 or 2 more, 1 or 2 less, hops on a number line, what changed, and stories. 100 picture questions with answers.
key_big: 1 more is the next number; 1 less is the number before.
key_sub: Start at the number you have and count on or back 1 or 2.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • 1 more: count on one. 6 and 1 more is 7.
  • 2 more: count on two. 6, then 7, 8.
  • 1 less or 2 less: count back. 6, then 5, 4.
  • Start at the number you have. You do not need to count everything again.

Examples

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Counting all over again from 1Start at the number you have and count on.
Counting back one too manySay the first number to yourself, then count back: 7 … 6, 5.
Mixing up more and lessMore means the group gets bigger. Less means it gets smaller.

faq.q: What does change in quantity mean in Kindergarten?
faq.a: Seeing what happens to a group when some are added or taken away, especially 1 or 2 more and 1 or 2 less, using real objects.
Children notice the pattern: 1 more is the next number when counting, and 2 more is two numbers on. This builds early addition.

faq.q: How can I practise at home?
faq.a: Put out a few toys, add or take away 1 or 2, and ask how many there are now and what changed.
Starting at the number you already have and counting forward, instead of counting everything from 1.
